title: DigCompEdu Check-In | Let the tool make the practice visible

qcReview.basis: Publisher’s English supplement dated 2 June 2023, © Ersoy et al., CC BY 4.0, was verified against the preserved SHA-256. The 4 prompts, 20 ordered options and item weights match the registered area; scoring follows the publication’s 0–4 option order. This independent report uses the project’s complete-response area sum (0–16); the original study reports 22-item total levels and did not validate independent area use. No source grading bands are imported.

interpretations.headline: Let the tool make the practice visible
interpretations.summary:
In a health-sciences practical, a group uploads its evidence for a decision before the debrief. Each student records one thing they would try differently next time. The instructor can open the discussion with what the group actually saw, while learners can compare their next attempt with their own plan.

The total describes how you reported using digital tools to add value in teaching, see collaboration, gather evidence and let learners monitor their progress. It does not show how learners performed. Choose one point in which a shared record, a check-in or a moment of learner reflection could make the experience clearer.

guidance.text: Choose one skill session and ask groups to document the evidence for a decision in one shared place. Agree what evidence belongs there, and leave identifiable clinical or learner information in approved systems.
In the debrief, ask each student to turn one observation into a next action. Before the next session, let them revisit that note and judge what changed.
If a digital tool is unreliable in the room or placement, plan a route that captures the same learning evidence with the resources learners can actually reach.

limitations: Ersoy, H., et al. (2024). Digital competence of faculty members in health sciences measured via self-reflection: current status and contextual aspects. PeerJ, 12, e18456. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.18456 ; Supplemental Information 1, Digital Competency Assessment Questionnaire for Academicians, 2 June 2023 (https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.18456/supp-1). Used under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Framework: Redecker, C. (2017), edited by Y. Punie, European Commission JRC, doi:10.2760/159770. This area-only presentation and feedback are project adaptations and imply no author or Commission endorsement.

This English reflection applies to adult higher-education faculty in health sciences. The original study used a convenience sample of 306 faculty members from six partner universities. The standalone area has no separate validation or local norms.

The area sum adds 4 equally weighted 0–4 items. Zero is a valid response; an omitted answer leaves the area result unavailable. No scale-wide total, A1–C2 level, percentile or individual certification is reported.
report.disclaimer: For your own professional learning in health-sciences higher education. This report describes self-reported digital teaching practice and supplies no basis for evaluating teaching performance, ranking faculty, or certifying competence.
